name: California fiscal notes — FTB revenue estimates for young child tax credit bills, as restated in Assembly Revenue and Taxation Committee analyses
organization: California Franchise Tax Board (estimates); Assembly Committee on Revenue and Taxation (publication)
access_note: ftb.ca.gov and leginfo.legislature.ca.gov return HTTP 403 to scripted fetches; the committee analyses on arev.assembly.ca.gov restate FTB's estimate verbatim in their FISCAL EFFECT paragraph and are fetchable.

model.name: Franchise Tax Board revenue estimates
model.method: General Fund revenue losses by State fiscal year (July-June) for the bill as introduced. The analyses do not state FTB's method (static or behavioural, accrual basis).
model.method_basis: FISCAL EFFECT paragraph of each analysis

bills.AB 397: Young child tax credit age limit from under 6 to under 10 (tax year 2025), 13 (2026), 16 (2027) and 19 (2028 on; 24 for students). Estimates: FY 2025-26 to FY 2027-28.
bills.AB 1690: Young child tax credit age limit of 6 plus the whole calendar years elapsed since January 1, 2026: under 7 in tax year 2027, under 8 in 2028 (18 from 2038). Estimates: FY 2027-28 and FY 2028-29.

scope_note: First tranche of the CA fiscal-note lane: FTB point estimates for bills PolicyEngine can express as a parameter change. The research map (2026-10-15) also lists LAO's CalWORKs grant costs and LAO's ranges (Proposition 3, the March 2026 tax options report) for later tranches. AB 2591 is not re-staged: the reform-validation registry already carries it (ca_fiscal_note, state.ca.ab2591).
diagnosis_upstream: FTB's estimating model is closed; a divergence classified as an external-model issue becomes a comparison memo.
